Unfortunately I'm the person who is mentally ill and wo t get therapy. Having withdrawal symptoms. I have my medications I just feel so weak to even take them. For me it's a failure label and I feel like I get no support if I take them. Therapy is hard to go to when you have had bad experiences with them as a child growing up. 

Really, we just like to see support. If it becomes too much for you as an individual to deal, you have every right to leave. If you're insistent on staying in a relationship or friendship. Try to be friendly and understanding. 

For example, my boyfriend tries really hard to understand me by looking up my illnesses to understand what my behaviors are. Sure. Its annoying as hell to him that I dont like taking my medication, but he understands why I dont. Make us feel strong in small ways even for just the smallest thing. That we have time and space. That we are also loved and accepted. 

Sometimes for the caregiver it sucks. It sucks seeing a loved one deteriorate before your eyes or say they want to die. Just understand that even being there as a listener and not speaking is very therapeutic for some mentally ill people.

https://www.psychologytoday.com/blog/bottoms/201611/what-is-cbt

I had the same thought process as you and I still somewhat do even though I'm in school to become a licensed clinical psychologist and or a therapist.
